cases.purpose: Verify the CPU1 I3C controller/target in the BMC-managed I3C topology using the platform/vendor specification and collect enumeration and error evidence.
preconditions: User provides the platform/BMC I2C-I3C specification, expected bus/controller and CPU1 target address or identifier, and the approved read-only procedure/criteria.
Confirm whether the probe is through BMC/Redfish/vendor tooling or the Ubuntu host; company scope treats I2C/I3C as BMC-domain functionality.
Confirm the required vendor package/tool and that it is approved for this platform.
pre_check_commands: Collect non-destructive BMC/Redfish inventory and existing I3C/I2C enumeration/status using the approved interface; preserve kernel/BMC/SEL baselines and do not clear logs.
If host-side visibility is explicitly supported, collect ls /sys/bus/i3c, ls /sys/bus/i3c/devices, and journalctl -k --no-pager without assuming a fixed bus number.
safety_checks: Do not guess the BMC bus, I3C address, CPU1 mapping, or target identity.
Do not run a write, firmware, reset, bus-recovery, or blind scan operation; use only the vendor-approved read-only probe.
Stop if the platform specification, package, interface, or recovery path is missing.
required_packages: Vendor-provided BMC/I3C diagnostic tool or approved i2c-tools/i3c support, only if compatible with the platform
cases.test_command: After the user supplies the BMC/I3C specification and approves the tool, run the vendor-approved read-only CPU1 I3C enumeration/status command with parameterized bus/address values; collect the specified response and error evidence.
risk_notes: The source procedure and criteria are placeholders, so no address, expected response, or pass condition can be inferred safely.

Blind i2cdetect/i3c probing can disturb or misidentify BMC-managed devices; the DeepSeek command hard-codes neither address but still lacks the platform-specific procedure and may call unavailable tooling.
expected_evidence: BMC/vendor tool version and command parameters supplied by the user
CPU1 I3C controller/target identity, address, status/response, and platform-specific comparison
Pre/post BMC/SEL and kernel evidence without clearing existing logs
post_check_commands: Repeat the approved read-only status query and collect the BMC/SEL and kernel-log delta; verify the BMC remains reachable and no unexpected bus/device error was introduced.
logs_to_collect: Connection/retry evidence if the BMC interface is remote
blocked_conditions: Missing or ambiguous BMC/I2C/I3C specification, bus/address/CPU1 identity, approved criteria, compatible package, or safe recovery procedure.
Only a blind scan or write-capable command is available.

deepseek_original_review.ai_commands: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh ... ls /sys/bus/i3c ... sudo i3cdetect -l ... dmesg ...
deepseek_original_review.ai_logs_output: I3C sysfs presence and dmesg i3c/i2c lines for CPU1 enumeration
deepseek_original_review.risk: I3C probing needs vendor tooling that may not be installed; report enumeration.

cases.gpt_second_review_findings: DeepSeek's PARTIAL classification is directionally appropriate, but its command is not sufficient evidence for this row: the procedure and criteria are only 'follow up spec', the BMC/I3C address and CPU1 mapping are unknown, and host sysfs visibility does not prove the BMC-domain target. Keep PARTIAL only as a guarded state: request the platform/vendor spec, address, package, and approved read-only procedure before execution; never blind-scan or guess the target.
cases.blast_radius: BMC-managed I3C/I2C bus, CPU1 management telemetry, BMC reachability, and related event logs.
cases.recovery_procedure: If the BMC becomes unreachable or a bus/device error appears, stop probing, preserve tool and BMC/SEL logs, wait for the specified timeout, and use the documented out-of-band BMC recovery path; do not reset the BMC or power-cycle without separate approval.
manual_steps: User/vendor supplies the BMC/I3C specification, expected address/identity, compatible package, and pass criteria.
User confirms the approved read-only procedure before the agent runs it.
cases.openhands_instruction: Ask for and validate the platform-specific BMC/I3C spec, CPU1 address/identity, package, and read-only command parameters. Show the resolved pre-checks and exact command to the user, wait for explicit OK, then run and return evidence only. End user decides PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.

cases.purpose: Verify by physical inspection that the PCIe-related components and connectors are seated correctly, can be safely unplugged and reconnected under the approved procedure, and that the expected device remains detected without new errors after the plug cycle.
preconditions: A qualified operator has physical access to the DUT and the approved PCIe/cable assembly procedure.
The expected PCIe device identity, slot or connector mapping, and post-cycle acceptance criteria are provided.
Power isolation, ESD controls, and the required operator photo/checklist locations are defined.
pre_check_commands: Before any physical action, preserve the current PCIe enumeration and kernel/BMC evidence with the approved read-only collection method; do not clear dmesg, syslog, or SEL.
safety_checks: Do not unplug or reconnect the PCIe assembly while energized unless the platform explicitly approves that hot-plug procedure.
Do not force a connector, continue after bent pins, abnormal power, smoke, damage, or loss of the management path.
Do not clear existing logs to create a baseline; record the baseline timestamp and collect only the approved post-cycle delta.
cases.test_command: A qualified operator inspects the PCIe components and connectors, performs the approved plug/reconnect cycle, and records seating, ease of connection, device identity, and photos. After the operator confirms the physical action is complete, the agent may collect the approved pre/post PCIe enumeration and kernel/BMC error evidence.
risk_notes: The source criteria are physical seating and plug-cycle behavior, so remote commands cannot establish the primary pass condition.
Incorrect handling can damage the PCIe card, slot, connector, cable, or chassis and can interrupt DUT availability.
The source procedure asks to clear logs, which would destroy historical evidence; a timestamped preserved baseline is required instead.
expected_evidence: Operator checklist and timestamped photos covering the PCIe components, connectors, and seating condition.
Pre/post identification of the expected PCIe device and approved detection result after the plug cycle.
Kernel, system, and BMC/SEL evidence for the post-action interval, with prior logs preserved.
post_check_commands: After operator confirmation, collect the approved PCIe enumeration, current device path or slot mapping, and kernel/BMC/SEL delta from the baseline timestamp.
Verify the expected device remains available and the management path is healthy before reporting the result.
logs_to_collect: Pre/post PCIe enumeration and device identity evidence
Kernel and BMC/SEL delta without deleting earlier records
blocked_conditions: No qualified operator or physical DUT access is available.
PCIe device identity, slot/connector mapping, approved plug-cycle procedure, or pass criteria are missing.
The platform does not approve the required physical cycle or the management path is lost after it.
Damage, abnormal power, bent pins, missing device, or new unexplained PCIe errors are observed.

cases.gpt_second_review_findings: DeepSeek's NO classification is correct for the source row because its acceptance criterion is physical seating and its procedure requires a plug cycle that cannot be performed or verified over SSH. GPT adds a safe evidence boundary: preserve the existing log history instead of following the source instruction to clear logs, require the expected PCIe identity and approved cycle procedure, and allow automation only for post-action enumeration and error evidence after operator confirmation.
cases.blast_radius: PCIe card, slot, connector and cable assembly, chassis availability, OS device enumeration, and the remote management path.
cases.recovery_procedure: Stop immediately on connector damage, bent pins, abnormal power, missing device, new unexplained PCIe errors, or loss of management access. Preserve the operator and system evidence, do not repeat the cycle or reboot automatically, and escalate to the hardware owner using the platform recovery procedure.
manual_steps: Operator performs the approved PCIe inspection and plug/reconnect cycle.
Operator records seating, device detection, physical discrepancies, and required photos.
cases.openhands_instruction: Do not attempt or claim the physical PCIe inspection or plug cycle. Validate the device identity, approved procedure, and read-only evidence commands; request the operator's confirmation and artifacts, then collect only the permitted post-action evidence. End user decides PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.

cases.purpose: Verify the physical power-connector assembly is correctly seated and can complete the approved unplug/reconnect cycle, then confirm the DUT remains powered and the expected components are detected without new errors.
preconditions: A qualified operator has physical access to the DUT and the platform-specific power-connector and power-isolation procedure.
The connector identity, expected PSU/power-path mapping, and post-cycle acceptance criteria are documented.
Power isolation, ESD controls, and the required operator checklist/photo locations are available.
pre_check_commands: Before physical handling, record the current BMC power/PSU telemetry, host availability, device enumeration, and kernel/BMC/SEL evidence using approved read-only collection; preserve existing logs.
safety_checks: Do not unplug or reconnect a power connector while energized unless the platform explicitly approves that operation and defines the required isolation.
Treat the connector as a high-current power path; stop for arcing, heat, odor, damaged insulation, bent contacts, abnormal PSU telemetry, or unexpected power loss.
Do not force the connector or clear dmesg, syslog, or SEL; use a timestamped baseline and collect the post-cycle delta.
cases.test_command: A qualified operator inspects the specified power connector and performs the approved power-isolated unplug/reconnect cycle, recording seating, connector condition, and photos. After operator confirmation, the agent may collect approved BMC/PSU telemetry, host/device availability, and kernel/BMC/SEL evidence for the post-cycle interval.
risk_notes: Power-connector handling can interrupt the DUT or damage a high-current connector, contact, cable, or PSU path.
The primary criterion is physical seating and connector condition, which cannot be verified by a remote agent.
The source procedure requests log clearing, which would remove useful evidence; the review requires preservation and timestamped deltas instead.
expected_evidence: Operator checklist and timestamped photos identifying the power connector, seating, and any physical defect.
Pre/post BMC power and PSU telemetry plus host availability and expected device enumeration.
Kernel, system, and BMC/SEL evidence for the post-cycle interval with pre-existing records preserved.
post_check_commands: After the operator confirms the cycle, collect the approved BMC/PSU status, host reachability, power-state telemetry, and expected device enumeration.
Collect kernel and BMC/SEL deltas from the baseline timestamp and confirm no unexplained power or management fault is present.
logs_to_collect: Kernel and BMC/SEL deltas without deleting earlier evidence
blocked_conditions: No qualified operator or physical DUT access is available.
Missing connector identity, power-path mapping, approved isolation/cycle procedure, or pass criteria.
Unsafe energized handling, damaged connector or insulation, abnormal heat/arcing/odor, or an unstable power path.
Loss of host or BMC access, unexpected power-off, missing device, or new unexplained power-related errors after the cycle.

cases.gpt_second_review_findings: DeepSeek's NO classification is correct for this row because the Power Connector acceptance criterion is physical seating and the procedure requires a human-performed plug cycle. This row has an electrical power-path hazard distinct from a data/PCIe connector: the operator must use the platform's isolation procedure and watch for power loss, arcing, heat, or abnormal PSU telemetry. GPT rejects clearing logs and limits automation to post-action power, availability, enumeration, and error evidence.
cases.blast_radius: Power connector and contacts, cable/PSU path, DUT power state, chassis availability, host devices, and BMC reachability.
cases.recovery_procedure: Stop on arcing, heat, odor, connector damage, abnormal PSU telemetry, unexpected power loss, or loss of management access. Preserve photos and all pre/post telemetry, do not repeat the cycle or force the connector, and escalate through the platform power-recovery procedure.
manual_steps: Operator performs the power-isolated physical inspection and approved unplug/reconnect cycle.
Operator records connector condition, seating, power behavior, and required photos.
cases.openhands_instruction: Do not attempt or claim the physical power-connector action. Validate the connector identity and approved isolation procedure, wait for operator confirmation and artifacts, then collect only the approved post-cycle BMC/PSU, availability, enumeration, and log evidence. cases.purpose: Verify the physical power-cable routing and seating meet the platform layout, do not impose unsafe strain or contact, and remain correctly connected through the approved plug-cycle inspection.
preconditions: A qualified operator has physical access to the DUT and the approved power-routing drawing or chassis service procedure.
The expected cable path, connector identity, bend/clearance requirements, and post-cycle acceptance criteria are defined.
Power isolation, ESD controls, and the required cable-routing checklist/photo locations are available.
pre_check_commands: Before physical handling, record current BMC power/PSU telemetry, host availability, device enumeration, and relevant kernel/BMC/SEL evidence without clearing existing logs.
safety_checks: Do not unplug, reroute, or reconnect a power cable while energized unless the platform procedure explicitly permits it.
Do not bend beyond the approved radius, pull against a connector, route across a fan or hot surface, or continue after chafing, pinching, exposed conductor, heat, or abnormal power telemetry.
Preserve the log baseline; do not clear dmesg, syslog, or SEL to hide a routing-induced fault.
cases.test_command: A qualified operator inspects the specified power-cable route, connector seating, bend radius, clearance, strain relief, and possible interference, then performs only the approved plug/reconnect cycle and records photos. After operator confirmation, the agent may collect approved power telemetry, device availability, and post-action error evidence.
risk_notes: Incorrect power routing can strain or damage connectors and insulation, obstruct cooling, contact hot or moving parts, or cause an intermittent or complete power fault.
Routing, clearance, and physical seating are not verifiable by remote commands.
The source asks to clear logs, but routing failures require preserved before/after evidence to correlate with power or thermal events.
expected_evidence: Operator routing checklist and timestamped photos showing connector seating, path, bend/clearance, strain relief, and any interference.
Pre/post power and PSU telemetry and confirmation that the expected host/devices remain available after the approved cycle.
Kernel and BMC/SEL delta for the post-action interval with historical logs preserved.
post_check_commands: After operator confirmation, collect approved BMC/PSU status, host reachability, device enumeration, and relevant thermal or fan status if the route passes through airflow areas.
Collect kernel and BMC/SEL deltas from the baseline timestamp and verify no unexpected power, thermal, or management event was introduced.
logs_to_collect: Kernel and BMC/SEL deltas without deleting earlier evidence
blocked_conditions: No qualified operator or physical access.
Missing routing drawing, connector identity, clearance/bend requirements, approved cycle procedure, or pass criteria.
Unsafe energized handling, cable damage, exposed conductor, pinch/chafe, blocked airflow, contact with a hot/moving part, or abnormal power behavior.
Loss of host/BMC access, unexpected power event, missing device, or new unexplained errors after the cycle.
